policies.summary: Pennsylvania has no state siting permit for wind or solar; municipalities (and counties where a municipality has no zoning) regulate them through zoning under the Municipalities Planning Code.
policies.statute_citation: Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, Act of July 31, 1968, P.L. 805, No. 247, §§ 601, 602, 619 (53 P.S. §§ 10601, 10602, 10619)

restrictions.description: Regulatory gap: current zoning ordinance does not address data centers, power generation plants, large-scale/accessory solar, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, or dispensaries, allowing any of them to be built anywhere in the township. Board Chairman Russell Ford emphasized the action was preemptive, not prompted by any pending application. Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 180-day expiry (~2027-01-09). Adopted via a unanimous June 22, 2026 motion and formalized by resolution at the July 13, 2026 meeting, the moratorium pauses applications for six business types (data centers, power generation plants, large-scale/accessory solar, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, dispensaries) while the township prepares a curative amendment to correct the declared invalidity. No news of an extension, adoption of the amendment, or repeal was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23. Legal basis: Adams Township Board of Supervisors resolution (a follow-up to the June 22, 2026 motion), invoking the municipal curative amendment process under the PA Municipalities Planning Code and declaring the zoning ordinance's exclusion of the six business types 'does not bear a substantial relationship to the public health, safety or morals' of residents, and that a sweeping ban 'cannot pass constitutional muster' and is therefore invalid (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).

restrictions.description: Regulatory gap: the zoning ordinance does not explicitly permit or provide standards for data centers or solar farms ('we don't have the protections in place'); adopted proactively, with no application pending, amid data-center and warehouse-development activity in neighboring Butler and Kline townships. Active as of 2026-09-23. Adopted unanimously on 2026-09-15, covering both data centers and solar farms (plus on-site power generation and accessory uses); the township hired Siana Law as special zoning counsel, with a draft corrective ordinance (addressing noise, buffers, power sources, and community benefits) expected the following month. No application for either use is currently pending. Legal basis: West Mahanoy Township Board of Supervisors resolution invoking the municipal curative amendment process under the PA Municipalities Planning Code, declaring the zoning ordinance invalid as it relates to data centers, solar farms, on-site power generation, and related accessory uses (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).

restrictions.long_description: In July 2024, the Smith Township Planning Commission began discussions to amend its solar and battery energy storage ordinance. On November 12, 2024, with the unanimous recommendation of the Planning Commission, the Board of Supervisors unanimously adopted the new ordinance 2024-5. The amendments include: increasing the setbacks from any occupied structures from 300 feet to 500 feet; adding Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to the Conservation District (C-D) as a conditional use and removing those from the Rural Residential (A-1) District; requiring an endangered species report; requiring a decommissioning plan to be submitted during land development and updated every three years instead of every five years; requiring a decommissioning bond to be set at 125% and reviewed every three years; and requiring a review from the Historical Society.

projects.description: In 2016, Atlantic Wind submitted a proposal to construct 37 wind turbines in Penn Forest Township on lands owned by the Bethlehem Municipal Authority.
projects.long_description: In 2016, Atlantic Wind submitted a proposal to construct 37 wind turbines in Penn Forest Township on lands owned by the Bethlehem Municipal Authority. The 2016 proposal was “deemed approved” when Penn Forest Township defaulted on deadline during the review process. Township residents filed a lawsuit challenging the deemed approval, but the approval was upheld in December 2017 by a Carbon County judge. In 2018, with the litigation on the first application still pending, Atlantic Wind submitted a modified application, this time seeking permission for only 28 turbines located farther from homes.

projects.description: During a series of 21 public hearings between January 2020 and March 2021, residents protested a 75-MW solar energy project proposed by Brookfield Solar I LLC that would span 1,000 acres across 26 different parcels of land in Mount Joy Township.
projects.long_description: During a series of 21 public hearings between January 2020 and March 2021, residents protested a 75-MW solar energy project proposed by Brookfield Solar I LLC that would span 1,000 acres across 26 different parcels of land in Mount Joy Township. At one hearing in August 2020, protestors argued that the town supervisor should be fired because he owns a solar lease. In June 2021, Mount Joy Township supervisors rejected the developer’s request for a conditional use permit to build a 391-acre stretch of the project along a major highway. On September 2, 2022, the Court of Common Pleas of Adams County, Pennsylvania upheld the denial of the permit, finding that the developer failed to provide sufficient analysis of adverse impacts on surrounding property owners, including stormwater runoff and glare.

projects.description: In November 2023, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court affirmed the denial of a permit for the Brookview Solar 1 project in Mount Joy Township.
projects.long_description: In November 2023, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court affirmed the denial of a permit for the Brookview Solar 1 project in Mount Joy Township. Project neighbors had opposed the development, collecting 950 signatures for a petition against the project.

projects.description: A pumped storage project faced opposition from local groups and environmentalists.
projects.long_description: York Energy Storage LLC plans to construct a 1.8-mile-long dam and flood 580 acres to create a hydroelectric facility designed to feed power into the regional grid. The project is named the Cuffs Run Pumped Storage Project and will have an estimated 1,000-acre footprint. In July 2023, a coalition of 17 nonprofits and local governments, along with Republican State Senator KrisDn Phillips-Hill of York, signed a letter urging federal regulators to reject the preliminary permit application for the project. The letter states that the “proposed project would destroy preserved farms, a regional scenic trail, and forested lands much needed to help protect the ecological health of this landscape and waterway.” In September 2023, FERC rejected the preliminary permit application due to deficiencies in the application; the application was refiled and accepted in February 2024.

projects.description: Enel Green Power’s plans to construct a 600-acre solar project in Dover Township encountered local opposition.
projects.long_description: Enel Green Power’s plans to construct a 600-acre solar project in Dover Township encountered local opposition. One group called Keep Dover Beautiful started a website to organize opposition against the project. The project was ultimately approved in 2022 after eight meetings.

projects.description: In February 2023, the Scranton Zoning Board denied zoning approval to ECA Solar for the construction of a solar farm on West Mountain.
projects.long_description: In February 2023, the Scranton Zoning Board denied zoning approval to ECA Solar for the construction of a solar farm on West Mountain. The Massachusetts-based company sought to re-zone 73 acres of land to install over 12,000 solar panels. Some residents had complained that the project would be visually disruptive and would lead to flooding from stormwater runoff.

projects.description: Vesper Energy's Firefly Solar project faced significant local opposition and was ultimately prohibited on agricultural land.
projects.long_description: Vesper Energy’s proposal to construct the 200-MW Firefly Solar project on prime farmland in North Beaver Township led to significant pushback, and the township ultimately prohibited solar development on agricultural land in 2021. Vesper continued to attempt to develop the project in Lawrence County.

projects.description: New Leaf Energy’s plans to construct a solar project on 23 acres of land zoned for suburban-residential development in Greenfield Township have encountered local opposition.
projects.long_description: New Leaf Energy’s plans to construct a solar project on 23 acres of land zoned for suburban-residential development in Greenfield Township have encountered local opposition. At a hearing in January 2023, residents expressed concerns about runoff and impacts to the environment, property values, and the town’s rural character. In February 2023, the township zoning board rejected the project.

projects.description: In June 2016, the Lehighton Water Authority formally denied Iberdrola Energy’s request to construct three wind turbines on Water Authority property in the area surrounding the Lehighton Borough’s drinking water supply.
projects.long_description: In June 2016, the Lehighton Water Authority formally denied Iberdrola Energy’s request to construct three wind turbines on Water Authority property in the area surrounding the Lehighton Borough’s drinking water supply. These turbines were meant to be part of a larger 100-MW wind energy project. Before the decision, some residents had raised concerns at a zoning meetingabout health, welfare, wildlife, and safety issues.

projects.description: In January 2005, Laurel Hill Wind Energy, LLC applied for a special exception to construct a 69-MW wind energy facility on land primarily within the County’s Resource Protection (RP) Zoning district.
projects.long_description: In January 2005, Laurel Hill Wind Energy, LLC applied for a special exception to construct a 69-MW wind energy facility on land primarily within the County’s Resource Protection (RP) Zoning district. The county Zoning Administrator granted the special exception by classifying the project as a “public service use,” prompting a nearby property owner to appeal. After multiple hearings, the Lycoming County Zoning Hearing Board (ZHB) ultimately denied the special exception, citing potential adverse impacts and inconsistencies with the RP’s purpose. Laurel Hill Energy appealed the denial to the Court of Common Pleas. In May 2007, the Court affirmed the ZHB’s denial. In November 2007, the Lycoming County Commissioners amended the zoning ordinance to permit wind energy facilities in certain districts, including the RP. In February 2008, Laurel Hill Energy applied for a zoning permit under the new ordinance, and its application was approved with conditions in May 2008. A month later, two local residents Arthur and Elke Plaxton, filed a substantive validity challenge against the ordinance amendments as invalid, arbitrary and unreasonable. In December 2009, the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania found no error in the ZHB’s decision and affirmed the denial of the challenge to the amendments. The project was allowed to proceed and was commissioned in October 2012.

projects.description: In April 2022, the North Annville Township Board of Supervisors denied an application for a conditional use permit for Lebanon Solar I, an 858-acre, 70-MW solar farm proposed by a subsidiary of Enel Green Power.
projects.long_description: In April 2022, the North Annville Township Board of Supervisors denied an application for a conditional use permit for Lebanon Solar I, an 858-acre, 70-MW solar farm proposed by a subsidiary of Enel Green Power. The developer appealed the decision to the Lebanon County Court of Common Pleas, which upheld the denial in January 2024 for failing to meet two conditions related to bonding requirements and stormwater management. In February 2024, the developer appealed the ruling to the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court. A resident opposed to the project also participated in the proceedings and filed an appeal. At public hearings, opponents expressed concerns about the proposed project’s proximity to their homes and its impact on property values, scenic views, and agriculture. Supporters argued that revenue from the leases would benefit farmers facing financial hardship, allowing them to keep their farms, and that solar arrays would be less permanent and intrusive than the warehouse distribution centers that have appeared in parts of the county.

projects.description: In September 2024, the Newton Township Supervisors voted to deny a plan by New Leaf Energy, a subsidiary of Borrego Solar Systems, to build around 12,000 solar panels on 24 acres of an old golf club.
projects.long_description: In September 2024, the Newton Township Supervisors voted to deny a plan by New Leaf Energy, a subsidiary of Borrego Solar Systems, to build around 12,000 solar panels on 24 acres of an old golf club. The project faced pushback during public hearings from dozens of local residents regarding harms to public health and welfare. In December 2024, Borrego filed an appeal of the supervisors’ decision.

projects.description: In December 2024, the Unity Township Zoning Board voted in a 3-2 decision to deny a special exemption necessary for the 34-acre Ninemile Run Solar project to be constructed.
projects.long_description: In December 2024, the Unity Township Zoning Board voted in a 3-2 decision to deny a special exemption necessary for the 34-acre Ninemile Run Solar project to be constructed. The project faced heavy opposition from local residents who raised concerns about noise. The developers began appealing the decision in late December.

projects.description: On July 31, 2024, the Pine Township Zoning Hearing Board rejected an application for a solar project that would have covered 20 acres in the township’s agricultural conservation zone.
projects.long_description: On July 31, 2024, the Pine Township Zoning Hearing Board rejected an application for a solar project that would have covered 20 acres in the township’s agricultural conservation zone. Local opponents spoke out against the project at a public meeting that ran for three hours ahead of the vote, raising concerns about impacts to property values.

projects.description: In August 2024, Lehman Township’s Zoning Hearing Board voted unanimously to deny a request from Susquehanna Solar to build a 46-acre solar farm in the municipal agricultural district.
projects.long_description: In August 2024, Lehman Township’s Zoning Hearing Board voted unanimously to deny a request from Susquehanna Solar to build a 46-acre solar farm in the municipal agricultural district. Following this decision, Susquehanna Solar canceled the project and decided against appealing the Board’s rejection.

projects.description: On August 21, 2024, the Nanticoke city council unanimously denied an application for a 40-acre solar project that would have been sited near a housing development.
projects.long_description: On August 21, 2024, the Nanticoke city council unanimously denied an application for a 40-acre solar project that would have been sited near a housing development. The project faced local opposition due to its proximity to residential areas.

projects.description: On August 15, 2022, two environmental groups filed an appeal with the Pennsylvania Environmental Hearing Board to challenge Pocono Township’s issuance of a permit to construct an 80-MW solar farm near Swiftwater Creek.
projects.long_description: On August 15, 2022, two environmental groups filed an appeal with the Pennsylvania Environmental Hearing Board to challenge Pocono Township’s issuance of a permit to construct an 80-MW solar farm near Swiftwater Creek. The groups alleged that deforestation on sloped land at the project site would cause runoff in Swiftwater Creek, one of Pennsylvania’s so called Exceptional Value (EV) streams and a tributary of a river that supplies drinking water to Monroe County residents.

projects.description: On November 4, 2024, the Palmyra Township Supervisors voted to reject an application by TotalEnergies to construct a 6-MW solar project.
projects.long_description: On November 4, 2024, the Palmyra Township Supervisors voted to reject an application by TotalEnergies to construct a 6-MW solar project. In denying the project, the supervisors echoed local concerns about visual impacts to the rural residential area, as well as property value impacts.

projects.description: Wilson Solar is seeking to develop an 80-MW solar project on approximately 1,129 acres of land in Erie County.
projects.long_description: Wilson Solar is seeking to develop an 80-MW solar project on approximately 1,129 acres of land in Erie County. Local residents have expressed opposition to the project based on concerns about visual and environmental impacts. A petition against the project had received over 280 signatures by December 2023. In November 2023, the Venango Township Planning Commission recommended that Venango Township supervisors reject the conditional use application for the solar farm. The supervisors delayed their planned vote on the proposal until January 2024 in response. In January 2024, the Board voted to deny the application and a rezoning request. In February 2024, Wilson Solar appealed the denial of the conditional use application to the Court of Common Pleas of Erie County and submitted a new conditional use permit to the township. As of September 2024, Venango Supervisors were considering the new application for a downsized project, which was being met by continued resistance from residents.

projects.description: In 2025, CVE North America proposed the 4.5-MW Derry Township Solar project to be located on approximately 60 acres of privately owned land in a rural neighborhood near New Alexandria.
projects.long_description: In 2025, CVE North America proposed the 4.5-MW Derry Township Solar project to be located on approximately 60 acres of privately owned land in a rural neighborhood near New Alexandria. In September 2025, the township supervisors held a public hearing at which the majority of attendees indicated that they opposed the project. The opponents have started an online petition against the project which highlights concerns about potential soil and groundwater contamination, impacts on wildlife and on the nearby Loyalhanna Creek, and impacts on the character of the community from the project.

projects.description: In 2023, Cornerstone Solar proposed the 200-MW Jefferson Solar project to be located on approximately 730 acres in Jefferson Township.
projects.long_description: In 2023, Cornerstone Solar proposed the 200-MW Jefferson Solar project to be located on approximately 730 acres in Jefferson Township. The project has faced opposition from local residents who have described it as an “eyesore” in their small municipality of 1,300 people and raised concerns about its potential impacts on the community’s rural character. In March 2026, the Jefferson Township Planning Commission recommended denial of a conditional use permit for the project on the basis that a small portion of the project site – less than 10 acres – does not meet the township’s subdivision criteria. The developer stated that the project proposal was subsequently revised to meet the township code. In April 2026, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) began excavation and remediation work  to remove barrels of toxic waste from a dump abandoned in the 1970s that partially overlaps with the project site. Opponents of the project have expressed hope that delays caused by the EPA’s cleanup efforts will discourage the developer from continuing with the project.
